population_estimates.note: Scholarly estimates range 6–14 million at peak; midpoint reported here.

description: Highland Andean empire ruling from Cuzco, ascendant after Pachacuti's defence of the city against the Chancas around 1438 and expanded under Pachacuti, Tupac Inca Yupanqui, and Huayna Capac to a north-south span of some 4,000 kilometres. The empire administered through an elaborate khipu-recorded fiscal system, a road network of about 40,000 kilometres, and resettlement (mitma) policies. By 1500 it had absorbed Chimor and the southern Andean polities; its succession crisis between Atahualpa and Huascar opened the way to Pizarro's 1532 conquest.

temporal.notes: Conventionally dated from Pachacuti's accession and his 1438 defence of Cuzco against the Chancas. The empire fell to the Spanish in 1533; Vilcabamba neo-Inca state to 1572. Within atlas scope to 1500.

geographic.notes: Capital Cuzco; the empire was administratively organised into four quarters (Antisuyu, Chinchaysuyu, Collasuyu, Cuntisuyu) meeting at the capital.

lifecycle_phases.description: Pachacuti defeats Chanca; conquers Lake Titicaca region and Chimor.
Topa Inca Yupanqui pushes the empire into modern Ecuador and Chile.
Huayna Capac founds northern co-capital at Quito; northern expansion.
Civil war between Huascar and Atahualpa fractures the state on the eve of Pizarro's arrival.

rise_factors.description: Mit'a labour tax, khipu record-keeping, and decimal administration (chunkas of 10 households) enabled state coordination without writing or money.
Vertical-archipelago economy linked highland, valley, and coastal ecological zones for complementary production.
Mit'a-conscripted armies of 30,000–80,000 supported by a stone road network of ~40,000 km made rapid mobilisation possible across two thousand kilometres of mountain terrain.

decline_factors.description: Civil war between Huascar and Atahualpa (1527–1532) over Huayna Capac's succession weakened the state immediately before Pizarro's 1532 arrival.
Smallpox arriving via Panama in 1525–28 killed Huayna Capac and ~50% of the indigenous population before any direct European contact in Tawantinsuyu.
